note: Words of agent context every session loads before reading any code. A ratchet: a count may never rise, and a fall is banked with `node scripts/check-context-budget.mjs --write`. See the module comment in scripts/check-context-budget.mjs.

raises.why: documents the four new tools this change adds (check:context-budget, agent:health, the concurrent check, and the two hooks); AGENTS.md is still 2,068 words below where this change found it
the dive-site briefing row now names both halves — which form writes each column and which beat reads it — after slice 7c deleted the reader and left eight authored columns reaching no diver
a new check:repo guard needs a row in the command table (check:type-ramp, #1229)
a new hard rule: text a human will copy is written unwrapped, so the copy does not arrive in a mailbox or support form full of hard breaks
a new check:repo guard needs a row in the command table (check:voice), and the brand-voice skill's description now names the voice tells so a session writing copy loads it

The two rows a session reads at the moment local running fails: what 'serving' means against Next's misleading 'Ready' (a 26s gap that reads as a wedge), that an announced memory restart is expected rather than a bug, that the dev lock is per-checkout so --port buys nothing, and that PGlite takes no lock so two openers of one .pglite silently fork it. Each was measured on 2026-09-03 and each previously cost a session an unguided hunt; the reasoning and the numbers are in ADR 20260903-the-dev-server-is-supervised and the debug skill, only the operative facts are here.

The debug skill's trigger now names a dev server that died, refuses to start, or serves stale data. Those are the symptoms this change added rows for, and they were the one class of failure whose sufferer had no reason to open the debug skill at all — an OOM-killed dev server reads as 'my change broke the app', not as 'a bug report or a red check'. Fourteen words to make the playbook load for the failure it now documents.

A project 'run' skill, and the one word that indexes it. Until now the generic global run skill was the authority at the exact moment a session launches this app, and it knows nothing about the twenty-six-second gap between Next's 'Ready' and the app answering, the supervisor's restart lines, the per-checkout dev lock, or that pnpm build beside pnpm dev silently forks the database. Every session was re-deriving a launcher and getting the same three things wrong; this is the fix for that being a recurring cost rather than a one-off.

The db:reset row now states the rule is enforced rather than remembered: a second opener of one .pglite is refused naming the process to stop, and a lock left by a killed server is taken over rather than obeyed. Both halves matter at the moment a session hits it — the first so an 'is already open by process N' refusal reads as working-as-intended, the second so nobody deletes the lock file by hand and re-opens the silent fork it exists to stop (ADR 20260903-one-process-per-pglite-directory).
The late-arrival buffer rule now names hasSailed/hasReturned and its guard; the long half (the fifteen spellings and the citation ring) went to docs/agents/repo-checks.md rather than here.
the pre-push coverage-guard rule (#1409): four CI failures in one afternoon came from guards that key off schema.ts from files nobody edits, so a focused run never selects them
